Screen environmental predictors for insufficient variance

Source: R/screen_egv_variance.R
screen_egv_variance.Rd

Calculates predictor standard deviations separately among presences, background records, and their combination, including spatial CV training partitions and (optionally) an independent test set.

Usage

screen_egv_variance(
  train,
  test = NULL,
  occ_folds = NULL,
  bg_folds = NULL,
  env = NULL,
  env_sample_n = 10000L,
  seed = NULL,
  sd_tol = 0,
  check_presences = TRUE,
  check_background = TRUE,
  check_combined = TRUE,
  presence_affects_selection = TRUE,
  include_test_bg = FALSE,
  check_test = FALSE,
  test_affects_selection = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

train

An SDMtune SWD object with presence and background data.

test

An optional independent-test SWD object.

occ_folds

An optional fold identifiers for TRAINING presences, in the order of train@pa == 1. A held-out fold is excluded in each CV check.

bg_folds

An optional fold identifiers for TRAINING background records, in the order of train@pa == 0. If omitted, all training backgrounds are reused in every CV partition (and the diagnostics state this explicitly).

env

An optional terra::SpatRaster representing the environmental domain.

env_sample_n

Whole integer >= 2 for random raster-cell sampling.

seed

NULL or one non-negative integer for reproducible env sampling; existing R random-number-generator state is restored.

sd_tol

Finite non-negative standard-deviation cutoff. Values <= sd_tol, or fewer than two finite observations, fail a check.

check_presences

Check presence-only subsets, default TRUE.

check_background

Check background-only subsets, default TRUE.

check_combined

Check joined presence/background subsets, default TRUE.

presence_affects_selection

If FALSE, presence-only failures are diagnostic-only. Defaults to TRUE for compatibility with previous screening.

include_test_bg

Whether to additionally check training and independent test backgrounds pooled together. Defaults to FALSE. The pooled check is diagnostic-only unless test_affects_selection = TRUE.

check_test

Whether to diagnose the independent test set separately (presences/background/combined according to the check_* switches). Defaults to FALSE. Its checks are diagnostic-only by default.

test_affects_selection

Explicitly allow checks involving independent test records to influence keep/remove. Defaults to FALSE to avoid test-informed preprocessing. Setting TRUE forfeits full test independence.

verbose

Print a summary (TRUE/FALSE).

Value

A named list containing:

keep

Predictors retained after variance screening.

remove

Predictors excluded by selection-relevant variance checks.

removed_by_check

Predictors removed by each selection-relevant check.

diagnostics

A data frame containing results of all performed variance checks, including failed and used_for_selection logical columns. The latter identifies whether each check contributes to predictor selection.

Details

Checks performed on training observations use only train@data. Supplying env adds an independent random environmental-domain check; it does not subsample or modify the supplied background observations.

CV checks exclude the held-out fold's presences and, when bg_folds is supplied, its background records. Without bg_folds, the full training background is shared across CV partitions. CV checks never inspect test.

When check_presences = FALSE, presence-only checks are omitted entirely. When presence_affects_selection = FALSE, presence-only checks are performed but do not influence predictor selection.

Each row in the returned diagnostics data frame contains a logical column named used_for_selection. This column indicates whether the corresponding variance check contributes to predictor selection. A predictor is included in remove if it fails at least one check for which used_for_selection is TRUE. Checks marked FALSE are retained for diagnostic purposes but do not influence keep or remove.

test_affects_selection = TRUE is an explicit opt-in and is generally inappropriate if test is meant as a final independent evaluation set. Select predictors within training data for each CV fold if estimating the predictive performance of an entire selection/model-fitting pipeline.

See also

SDMtune::prepareSWD(), terra::spatSample()

Examples

# Self-contained example with package dependencies, no external files.
r <- terra::rast(nrows = 10, ncols = 10, xmin = 0, xmax = 10,
                 ymin = 0, ymax = 10)
terra::values(r) <- seq_len(terra::ncell(r))
names(r) <- "gradient"
r2 <- r
terra::values(r2) <- rep(seq_len(10), each = 10)
names(r2) <- "stripes"
env <- c(r, r2)
p <- data.frame(x = c(1.5, 3.5, 5.5, 7.5),
                y = c(1.5, 3.5, 5.5, 7.5))
a <- data.frame(x = c(0.5, 2.5, 4.5, 6.5, 8.5),
                y = c(8.5, 6.5, 4.5, 2.5, 0.5))
train <- SDMtune::prepareSWD("Example species", env, p = p, a = a,
                             verbose = FALSE)
result <- screen_egv_variance(train, occ_folds = c(1, 1, 2, 2),
                              env = env, env_sample_n = 50,
                              seed = 1, verbose = FALSE)
result$keep
#> [1] "gradient" "stripes" 
head(result$diagnostics)
#>      check subset data_source      group fold used_for_selection variable
#> 1 training    all    training  presences <NA>               TRUE gradient
#> 2 training    all    training  presences <NA>               TRUE  stripes
#> 3 training    all    training background <NA>               TRUE gradient
#> 4 training    all    training background <NA>               TRUE  stripes
#> 5 training    all    training   combined <NA>               TRUE gradient
#> 6 training    all    training   combined <NA>               TRUE  stripes
#>   n_finite        sd failed reason
#> 1        4 23.237900  FALSE passed
#> 2        4  2.581989  FALSE passed
#> 3        5 34.785054  FALSE passed
#> 4        5  3.162278  FALSE passed
#> 5        9 28.416544  FALSE passed
#> 6        9  2.738613  FALSE passed
